  "hypothesis": "Predicted that nonface line patterns with salient Gestalt information would be processed holistically, yielding a significant congruency effect and a significant Congruency by Alignment interaction in a composite task, comparable to human faces.",
  "design": "within-subject, with factors Task (faces vs. line patterns), Alignment (aligned vs. misaligned), Congruency (congruent vs. incongruent), and Target (same vs. different top parts)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Visual stimuli consisting of composite human faces versus composite line patterns possessing salient Gestalt information (connectedness, closure, continuity, and emergence)",
  "outcome_measure": "Response sensitivity (d') in same/different judgments of the top parts of composite stimuli",
  "population_and_setting": "22 participants tested in a laboratory setting",
  "sample_size_total": 22,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "22 people registered to participate; not otherwise specified",
  "analysis_plan": "Repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) on response sensitivity (d') with factors alignment, congruency, and task, followed by tests of simple main effects (congruency effects in aligned and misaligned conditions)",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants performed two composite tasks in counterbalanced order within a single session. Each trial presented a target stimulus followed by a mask and a second stimulus (aligned or misaligned), and participants judged whether the top parts were the same or different while ignoring bottom parts."
